rule: A value is written after the equals sign as `line`, and the bot's dotenv reads that line back as the same value. A case marked lossy is a value no spelling can carry: the bot reads something different.

cases.name: a plain word is written as it is
an empty value is written as nothing
spaces inside a value need no quotes
spaces at the ends are kept by single quotes
a # with a space before it is kept by single quotes
a # with no space before it is kept by single quotes
a value starting with # is kept by single quotes
a value starting with a double quote is kept by single quotes
a value wrapped in double quotes keeps them inside single quotes
a value starting with a single quote is kept by double quotes
a single quote inside a value needs no quotes
a double quote inside a value needs no quotes
a single quote and a # are kept by double quotes
both quote kinds and a # are kept by backticks
a single quote, a # and a written backslash n are kept by backticks, which leave the backslash n alone
spaces at the ends with a single quote inside are kept by double quotes
a Telegram token is written as it is
a path with spaces is written as it is
a command template is written as it is
a command template with a quoted placeholder is written as it is
an equals sign needs no quotes
a backslash needs no quotes
a backslash and a # are kept by single quotes
a # with all three quote kinds cannot be written so that the bot reads it back
a #, a single quote, a backtick and a written backslash n cannot be written so that the bot reads it back
